observations.observation: The metric is quadratic weighted kappa on integer scores 1-6, so threshold rounding of blended continuous predictions is appropriate.
observations.evidence: task.md Evaluation section describes QWK; all predict_*.py scripts already use OptimizedRounder.predict with 5 thresholds.

observations.observation: The current version v136 scores lower than the best earlier versions.
The drop in v134-v136 coincides with switching away from the large-model ensembles.
observations.evidence: history.md: v134 removed tuned weights (0.80343), v136 switched to DeBERTa-v3-small exp305 checkpoints (0.80526); earlier large-model runs scored 0.822-0.828.

observations.observation: The current code runs only one model pipeline at inference time.
observations.evidence: current_code.py: only the predict_separated.py cell (deberta-v3-small) is uncommented; all other predict_* cells are commented out.

observations.observation: The current code blends raw predictions across different model families before rounding.
observations.evidence: Each predict_*.py script averages only its own fold checkpoints and writes a rounded submission.csv; no script saves unrounded predictions and no blending cell exists.

observations.observation: The exp320 PET-large run with tuned thresholds was the single best scoring configuration in history.
observations.evidence: history.md v129: predict_pet2 with exp320-large-last checkpoints and last weight 4.87535 scored 0.82845.

observations.observation: The exp306b ordinal-large and exp302c two-stage-large runs each reached competitive scores on their own.
observations.evidence: history.md v130 (exp306b-large-clean-last) 0.82607; v122 (exp302c-large-scale-best with sigmoid rescale) 0.82435.

observations.observation: Hand-tweaking blend thresholds without a model change has already been tried repeatedly.
observations.evidence: history.md v124->v125, v133->v134, v134->v135 only changed weights, with scores 0.819, 0.803, 0.808.

observations.observation: The predict_pet2.py script writes predictions in sample_submission order without sorting by length.
observations.evidence: current_code.py predict_pet2.py: no ds.sort, sub read from sample_submission.csv and assigned preds directly; predict_ordinal/exp302 sort by length and merge on sorted_ids.

observations.observation: The three chosen pipelines output raw predictions on a comparable 1-6 scale.
observations.evidence: predict_pet2 multiplies by 5 and adds 1; predict_ordinal sums sigmoids and adds 1; predict_exp302 rescales *5+1 when config do_scale is set (exp302c-large-scale-best config, v122).

action_summary: Replaced the single DeBERTa-v3-small exp305 inference (LB 0.805) with a three-member ensemble of the strongest large-model pipelines from history: exp320 PET-large (predict_pet2), exp306b ordinal-large clean-last (predict_ordinal) and exp302c two-stage large scale-best (predict_exp302), each averaging its four fold checkpoints. Modified these three scripts to additionally write unrounded raw predictions (submission_<name>_raw.csv). Added a new blend.py that merges the raw predictions on essay_id, takes a weighted average (0.40/0.35/0.25, weighted toward the historically best member), uses the correspondingly weighted average of each member's previously tuned QWK thresholds, applies OptimizedRounder, clips to 1-6 and writes submission.csv. Missing members are skipped gracefully so the pipeline still produces a submission.
